title: P2.15d Wire live navigation and plan approval
description: Control Room navigation remains inert and plan approval is deliberately disabled even as handshake/poll fixes land. Wire the production route and approval command only where server affordances authorize it.
definitionOfDone: Re-measure dirty Cordum shell/navigation/live dispatch ownership and the production plan-approval command/affordance; block rather than collide or fabricate an approval route.
Navigation buttons drive one typed route source of truth with durable goal/run identifiers; unavailable destinations are explicitly disabled rather than inert.
Plan approval calls the real typed command only when the server affordance authorizes it. Success refreshes durable state; refusal stays visible and pins exact code/layer.
UI tests cover navigation, disabled affordances, success/refusal, no fixed goal/run ids, and nonzero exact route/affordance rosters.
taskRails: Re-measure current HEAD, exact-path porcelain, and live ownership before planning or editing; adopt provenance-verified foreign WIP or block on collision.
Use production-reachable evidence, exact stable refusal code and layer where applicable, nonzero tests, mutation drills for security boundaries, and explicit-pathspec commits only.
Do not treat a caller-shaped HUMAN flag or enabled button as approval authority. Preserve active handshake/poll task ownership.

comments.content:
VERIFY-OR-BLOCK MEASUREMENT (2026-08-25, HEAD e59fa4d7732e2ac0395b7e01750a9198c9c756f0):
1. Navigation ownership/collision. `cordum-app.tsx`, `cordum-app.test.tsx`, `cordum-shell.tsx`, `cordum-shell.test.tsx`, and `shell/nav-rail.tsx` are all tracked-modified foreign WIP. CordumApp hard-codes `activeNav="goals"` and supplies no `onNavigate`; the rail merely enables every destination when any callback exists, not per-route availability. The typed route source required by DoD 2 does not exist (`rg` finds only NavId/onNavigate). Downstream task-7e605144... explicitly reserves cordum-app.tsx and cordum-app.test.tsx for P2.15c integration; planning this row over those paths before it lands is a live collision.
2. Approval route is absent, not merely unwired. `approve-plan.tsx` is clean and deliberately read-only/disabled. The daemon's offered `approval.decide` NextAllowedCommand contains command identity, target, schema and expectedVersion only. `planning-run-read.ts` returns runId/lifecycle/submissionHash plus sealed plan, acceptance and authority hashes; it does NOT return an approval record, activation witness or graph revision input.
3. The production handler `apps/daemon/src/planning/planning-services.ts:231-309` requires caller payload fields `runId`, `record`, `command`, `activation`, and `graphRevisionRef`; it checks record.actor against the authenticated principal, exactRevisionHash against durable submissionHash, applies the approval command, verifies the run binding, then activates. The browser has no production reader for the authoritative record/activation values. The only current browser payload is `DEV_PAYLOADS["approval.decide"]` in dirty `live-dispatch.ts`, explicitly documented as fixture-shaped/fabricated. Using it would violate this row's no-fabricated-route and no caller-shaped HUMAN authority rails.
4. Dispatch WIP is also not safe to adopt: `live-dispatch.ts` is tracked-modified at 506 physical lines and duplicates a new untracked `live-command-dispatch.ts` (167 lines). It is involved in broad foreign goal/live work; a clean checkout has no extracted module.
Required resolution before UI planning: (a) complete P2.15c or explicitly reassign its CordumApp paths, and (b) land a production daemon-owned approval-intent/command composition seam that returns or server-derives every non-operator approval/activation fact while preserving `approval.decide`'s authenticated human-review gate. Then this UI row can consume the daemon-minted affordance, submit only the typed operator decision, refresh the run/surface after success, and render exact refusal code/layer. Without that seam, an enabled button must remain disabled.
